statements.claim: The Dirichlet-box lattice action equals ε² times the quadratic form of the matrix dirOp.
Mass lower bound: the Dirichlet action is at least m₀² ε² Σ_x φ_x².
For m₀ ≠ 0 the Dirichlet operator dirOp is a positive definite matrix.
Off-diagonal entries of dirOp are ≤ 0 (Z-matrix property).
For m₀ ≠ 0 the Dirichlet Green function dirGreen = dirOp⁻¹ is entrywise nonnegative (dirOp is a Stieltjes matrix).
For m₀ ≠ 0 the Dirichlet Green function is positive definite.
Gaussian integration by parts on ℝ^ι: for a positive definite A and F differentiable with F and ∂_x F bounded by C·exp(a Σ|φ_i|), ∫ (Aφ)_x F(φ) ρ_A(φ) dφ = ∫ ∂_x F(φ) ρ_A(φ) dφ, ρ_A = exp(−½⟨φ, Aφ⟩).
Covariance form of Gaussian integration by parts: ∫ φ_x F ρ_A = Σ_y (A⁻¹)_{xy} ∫ ∂_y F ρ_A, for F with exponentially bounded derivative.
Diagonal entries of the Dirichlet operator: dirOp x x = 4/ε² + m₀².
Nearest-neighbour entries of the Dirichlet operator equal −1/ε².
All entries of dirOp between distinct non-neighbouring sites vanish.
Covariance of the Dirichlet free field: with weight exp(−½ dirAction), ⟨φ_x φ_y⟩ = ε⁻² dirGreen x y.
Diagonal bound for the Dirichlet Green function: dirGreen x x ≤ 1/m₀².
The Dirichlet Green function decreases entrywise as m₀² increases.

Griffiths I, general form: for an even nonnegative single-site weight and polynomials with nonnegative coefficients, the integral of the observable times exp(interaction) times the product weight is ≥ 0.
Griffiths' first inequality: for an even nonnegative single-site weight w and ferromagnetic couplings J ≥ 0, ∫ ∏_x φ_x^{a_x} · exp(Σ J_xy φ_x φ_y) ∏_x w(φ_x) dφ ≥ 0.
Griffiths I remains true with a nonnegative external field added to the ferromagnetic interaction.
Griffiths' first inequality with site-dependent even nonnegative weights w_x and couplings J ≥ 0: ∫ ∏ φ_x^{a_x} exp(Σ J_xy φ_x φ_y) ∏ w_x(φ_x) ≥ 0.
Griffiths I for the quartic Dirichlet-box weight: for all m₀, λ and exponents a, ∫ ∏_x φ_x^{a_x} · dweight(φ) dφ ≥ 0.
Ferromagnetic decomposition: the Dirichlet-box weight equals exp(Σ_{x,y} J_xy φ_x φ_y) ∏_x w_x(φ_x) with nearest-neighbour couplings J ≥ 0 and explicit site weights.
For m₀ ≠ 0 and λ ≥ 0 the quartic Dirichlet-box weight is integrable.
For m₀ ≠ 0 and λ ≥ 0 the quartic Dirichlet-box partition function is strictly positive.
Griffiths I for the normalised quartic box measure: every monomial moment ⟨∏ φ_x^{a_x}⟩ is ≥ 0.
For λ ≥ 0, m₀ ≠ 0 every monomial times the quartic Dirichlet-box weight is integrable.
Griffiths I in genuine form: for λ ≥ 0, m₀ ≠ 0 the quartic box Gibbs measure is a probability measure, each monomial is integrable, and its expectation equals the normalised moment and is ≥ 0.
Sign-averaging lemma for doubled variables: if W ≥ 0 is invariant under the doubled sign-flip group and the group average of f is ≥ 0 pointwise, then ∫ f W ≥ 0.
Griffiths II in the cone (unnormalised): for site-dependent even weights, Q with nonnegative coefficients, A, B in the cone 𝒞 and ρ = e^Q ∏ w_x, (∫ABρ)(∫ρ) ≥ (∫Aρ)(∫Bρ), given integrability.
Griffiths' second inequality holds for site-dependent even weights and J ≥ 0 whenever the monomial moments are integrable; no Ginibre-type condition beyond evenness is needed.
Griffiths II for the quartic Dirichlet-box weight, for λ ≥ 0, m₀ ≠ 0.
Griffiths II for the normalised quartic box measure: for λ ≥ 0, m₀ ≠ 0, ⟨φ^a φ^b⟩ ≥ ⟨φ^a⟩⟨φ^b⟩ for all monomials.
The Simon–Lieb bond coupling bondJ u v = −ε² dirOp(m₀=0) u v is nonnegative.
If bondJ u v ≠ 0 then the physical sup-distance between u and v is at most the lattice spacing ε.
Splitting the action across a region B: dirAction φ = dirAction(φ|_B) + dirAction(φ|_{Bᶜ}) − 2 Σ_{u∈B, v∉B} J_uv φ_u φ_v.
Factorisation across ∂B (BFS (6.2)): the box weight equals the decoupled weight times exp(Σ_{u∈B,v∉B} J_uv φ_u φ_v) times an explicit constant.
Zero-coupling factorisation: the decoupled integral of G(φ|_B) is the region-B integral times the complement partition function, with no integrability hypothesis.
The decoupled two-point function of fields in B equals the Dirichlet region two-point function regionTwoPt B (given a nonzero complement partition function).
BFS (6.2): the box two-point function equals ⟨φ_x φ_y Φ⟩_dec / ⟨Φ⟩_dec with Φ = exp(Σ_{u∈B,v∉B} J_uv φ_u φ_v).
Conditional: Simon–Lieb, Griffiths I for regions, a small boundary sum < 1 and a uniform base bound imply exponential decay of the two-point function uniformly in the cutoff and volume.
Conditional end-to-end: the M6 inputs plus Newman's inequality and |ZD| ≤ 1 give finite-cutoff clustering at some rate m > 0.
Shifting the local time at site i by s multiplies the weight W_τ by an explicit exponential factor in f(φ_i²/2+τ_i+s) − f(φ_i²/2+τ_i).
One-site integration by parts at fixed local time: ∫ ∂_i R · W_σ = ∫ R · φ_i f′(φ_i²/2 + σ_i) · W_σ, given integrability.
Integrability against W_τ of a continuous observable is preserved when the local time at one site is raised by s ≥ 0.
One-site local-time integration by parts: for W_τ = ∏ e^{−f(φ_x²/2+τ_x)}, f(u) = au + bu², ∫ φ_i R W_τ = ∫_0^∞ ds ∫ ∂_i R · W_{τ+s e_i}, under continuity and integrability assumptions.
BFS form: with [F]_τ = ∫ F e^{Q_K} W_τ and J = K + Kᵀ, [φ_i G]_τ = ∫_0^∞ ds [∂_i G + Σ_j J_ij φ_j G]_{τ+s e_i}.
For τ ≥ 0 and b ≥ 0, W_τ ≤ e^{−Σ_x f(τ_x)} W_0.
The BFS coupling J_xy = Jnn_xy + Jnn_yx equals the Simon–Lieb coupling bondJ_xy for x ≠ y.
The quartic Dirichlet weight equals a constant times e^{Σ Jnn φφ} · W_0 with site exponent f(s) = αs + βs² (the Wick constant factors out).
For m₀ ≠ 0, λ ≥ 0, τ ≥ 0, every observable bounded by C e^{aΣ|φ|} (all polynomials) is integrable against the τ-shifted quartic weight.
R2 for the quartic Dirichlet box: for m₀ ≠ 0, λ ≥ 0, τ ≥ 0, [φ_i G]_τ = ∫_0^∞ ([∂_i G]_{τ+se_i} + Σ_j J_ij [φ_j G]_{τ+se_i}) ds for G of exponential-linear growth with such a derivative.
The same local-time integration by parts with the Simon–Lieb coupling Σ_{j≠i} bondJ_ij.
Raising site masses lowers cone expectations: for even weights w_x ≥ 0, Q with nonnegative coefficients, H in the cone 𝒞, γ ≥ 0 and ρ′ = e^{−Σγ_xφ_x²}ρ, (∫Hρ′)(∫ρ) ≤ (∫Hρ)(∫ρ′), given integrability.
Volterra positivity lemma: if J ≥ 0 has row sums ≤ r < c, D_i(τ) = ∫_0^∞ E_i(τ,s) ds with E_i(τ,s) ≥ Σ_k J_ik D_k(τ+se_i), and −D_i(τ) ≤ M e^{−cΣτ}, then D ≥ 0 on [0,∞)^ι.
Griffiths II monotonicity in local times: for K ≥ 0, b ≥ 0, τ ≤ τ′ and H in the cone 𝒞, [H]_{τ′}[1]_τ ≤ [H]_τ[1]_{τ′}, i.e. ⟨H⟩_τ decreases in τ.
Local-time integration by parts for a general pair matrix K and admissible G: [φ_i G]_τ = ∫_0^∞ ([∂_i G]_{τ+se_i} + Σ_j (K_ij+K_ji)[φ_j G]_{τ+se_i}) ds.
For admissible H, s ↦ [H]_{τ+s e_i} is integrable on (0, ∞).

Strong Gaussian domination (BFS Thm 5.1), abstract finite-dimensional form: for ferromagnetic K ≥ 0, site exponent au+bu², and admissible G with derivatives in the cone 𝒞, [φ_i G]_0 ≤ Σ_j ⟨∂_j G⟩_0 [φ_i φ_j]_0.
For the quartic box (m₀ ≠ 0, λ ≥ 0), cone expectations ⟨H⟩_τ decrease in each local time τ_x.
Row sums of the BFS coupling are at most 4: Σ_y J_xy ≤ 4.

Strong Gaussian domination for the quartic Dirichlet box (m₀ ≠ 0, λ ≥ 0): ⟨φ_i G⟩ ≤ Σ_j ⟨∂_j G⟩⟨φ_i φ_j⟩ for G of exponential-linear growth whose derivatives lie in the cone 𝒞 (e.g. polynomials with nonnegative coefficients).

Conditional smeared decay: Simon–Lieb with local term, Griffiths I for regions, boundary sum ≤ γ < 1 and region susceptibility ≤ A imply the smeared two-point function against 0 ≤ w ≤ 1 supported at distance ≥ N(l+1) is ≤ A/(1−γ)·γ^N.
The smeared M6 consumer: the four inputs (Simon–Lieb with local term, region Griffiths I, small boundary sum, region susceptibility) give uniform smeared exponential decay of the two-point function.
Conditional clustering with smeared decay: a Newman-type bound plus uniform smeared decay of G give finite-cutoff clustering of the generating functional ZD.
Conditional end-to-end (smeared): the M6' inputs and Newman's inequality with G = twoPt give finite-cutoff clustering at some rate m > 0.
For m₀ ≠ 0, λ ≥ 0, every admissible observable with envelope 1 + e^{bdryCoupling} is integrable against the decoupled measure e^{Q_decJ} W_0.
Local-time expectations for the decoupled coupling decJ equal explicit constant multiples of integrals against the decoupled weight decWeight_B.
For x, j ∈ B the region two-point function regionTwoPt B x j equals the decoupled ratio [φ_x φ_j]_0 / [1]_0 (m₀ ≠ 0, λ ≥ 0).
Simon–Lieb inequality with local term for the quartic Dirichlet box (m₀ ≠ 0, λ ≥ 0): for x ∈ B and any y, twoPt x y ≤ regionTwoPt B x y + Σ_{u∈B} Σ_{v∉B} bondJ u v · regionTwoPt B x u · twoPt v y.
The proposition SimonLiebIneq' m₀ λ (Simon–Lieb with local term, all cutoffs, regions and sites) holds for every m₀ ≠ 0 and λ ≥ 0.
The Simon–Lieb inequality SimonLiebIneq m₀ λ (for y ∉ B) holds for every m₀ ≠ 0 and λ ≥ 0.
SimonLiebTarget: the Simon–Lieb inequality holds for all m₀ ≠ 0 and λ ≥ 0.
Ahlswede–Daykin four functions theorem for Lebesgue measure on ℝ^ι, ι any finite type.
FKG inequality: for an integrable log-supermodular density ρ ≥ 0 on ℝ^ι and bounded monotone F, G, (∫FGρ)(∫ρ) ≥ (∫Fρ)(∫Gρ).
The Dirichlet-box weight satisfies the FKG lattice condition (log-supermodularity), for all n, k, m₀, λ, P.
FKG for the normalised quartic box measure: for λ ≥ 0, m₀ ≠ 0 and bounded measurable monotone F, G, ⟨FG⟩ ≥ ⟨F⟩⟨G⟩.
FKG for the quartic box Gibbs measure: ∫FG dμ ≥ ∫F dμ · ∫G dμ for bounded measurable monotone F, G (λ ≥ 0, m₀ ≠ 0).
FKG for bounded monotone observables extends (by truncation) to integrable monotone observables with integrable product.
Abstract Newman comparison: for an FKG measure, if G₁ ± F and G₂ ± H are increasing (F, H bounded, G₁, G₂, G₁G₂ integrable), then |Cov(F,H)| ≤ Cov(G₁,G₂).
The quartic Dirichlet-box Gibbs measure satisfies FKG for bounded measurable monotone observables (λ ≥ 0, m₀ ≠ 0).
For c, d ≥ 0, Cov(Σ c_x φ_x, Σ d_y φ_y) ≤ Σ_x Σ_y c_x d_y ⟨φ_x φ_y⟩ under the quartic box Gibbs measure (uses Griffiths I).
Newman's inequality for the quartic Dirichlet box (λ ≥ 0, m₀ ≠ 0): ‖ZD(f+g) − ZD(f)ZD(g)‖ ≤ 4 Σ_x Σ_y ε²|f(x)| ε²|g(y)| ⟨φ_x φ_y⟩ for all n, k, f, g.

With Newman's inequality discharged: Simon–Lieb with local term, Griffiths I for regions, small boundary sum γ < 1 and region susceptibility give finite-cutoff clustering at some rate m > 0 (λ ≥ 0, m₀ ≠ 0).
The finite-cutoff generating functional ZD has norm at most 1.
Diagonal extraction: a uniformly bounded sequence of complex functions, equicontinuous w.r.t. ρ on a space with a countable ρ-dense subset, has a pointwise convergent subsequence.
For λ ≥ 0, m₀ ≠ 0, ‖ZD f − ZD g‖ ≤ ⟨|φ(f − g)|⟩ uniformly in the cutoffs n, k.
Conditional on uniform equicontinuity of ZD in a finite Schwartz seminorm and Schwartz separability, ZD has a limit point.
Cauchy–Schwarz against the Gibbs measure: ⟨|φ(h)|⟩ ≤ ⟨φ(h)²⟩^{1/2}.
Under a uniform susceptibility bound K, ⟨φ(h)²⟩ ≤ K·M·ε² Σ_x |h(x)| for |h| ≤ M.
Uniform smeared exponential decay (rate m > 0) of the two-point function implies a uniform susceptibility bound sup_x ε² Σ_y |⟨φ_x φ_y⟩| ≤ K.
Riemann-sum bound for Schwartz functions: ε² Σ_x |h(x)| ≤ 1024 ‖h‖_{4,0}, uniformly in the cutoffs.
A uniform susceptibility bound K gives uniform equicontinuity: ‖ZD f − ZD g‖ ≤ 128 (max K 0)^{1/2} ‖f − g‖_{4,0} uniformly in n, k (λ ≥ 0, m₀ ≠ 0).
Uniform smeared decay and Schwartz separability give a limit point of ZD.
The hypotheses of the smeared M6 consumer and Schwartz separability give a limit point of ZD.
Griffiths I holds for the Dirichlet region measures, for all m₀ and λ.

Conditional on the two node-M5 inputs (boundary sum ≤ γ < 1 and region susceptibility ≤ A), finite-cutoff clustering holds at some rate m > 0 for m₀ ≠ 0, λ ≥ 0; Simon–Lieb, Newman and region Griffiths I are proved.
Conditional on the node-M5 inputs and Schwartz separability, ZD has a limit point.
